findings.reason: the design's stated prior art is not the mechanism it needs, so the reuse citation cannot justify the new module and the plan should cite and extend the actual geometric-moment owner.
findings.text: §2 (plan.html:42) names polygon_analytic_flux_moments as the machinery that "integrates the geometric moments of the region exactly", but opening the function shows it returns fixed-section flux-kernel blocks (uniform, radial and vertical rows of the Biot kernel over the polygon's edges) and computes only a centroid; no polygon area/first/second moment integrator lives in nova/biot.

findings.reason: extending the existing moment owner rather than forking a module removes a whole parallel implementation and the drift risk between three moment tables.
findings.text: _traced_polygon_moments already computes the polygon's area and first and second moments in JAX with the same orientation handling the design is proposing to write again; the plan introduces nova/equilibrium/polygon_moments.py (polygon_monomial_moments, line 141) as a parallel body, and a third body (_straight_edge_monomial_moments, clip_quadrature.py:155) carries production. A duplicate of shared infrastructure is a finding naming the owner to extend: separatrix_clip._traced_polygon_moments.

findings.reason: the plan should either extend the owner the production path uses, or state why a second module is needed, rather than land two implementations of one reduction.
findings.text: the landed design locked decision moment-integration to "closed-form polygon moments" in the new module, yet production reaches the endpoint-recurrence body in clip_quadrature.py:155 and the new module is imported only by benchmarks/exact_clip_closed_form_floor.py; the plan therefore authored a mechanism decision that its own shipped path did not take, leaving a tested but unused parallel module.

findings.reason: collapsing to one owner behind one interface is the depth the design claims and does not deliver while three copies stand.
findings.text: three separate polygon-moment reductions now coexist (separatrix_clip.py:850, clip_quadrature.py:155, polygon_moments.py:141), each with its own edge-weight/binomial/orientation logic and its own tests, so the moment machinery is spread across parallel bodies rather than buried behind one interface.

findings.reason: the section must account for the public surface it adds in its own text, and retiring the duplicate moment modules would discharge it.
findings.text: the section adds a public module (__all__ exporting LOCAL_MONOMIAL_POWERS, QUADRATIC_POWERS, PolygonDensityMoments, polygon_density_moments, polygon_monomial_moments) and its text retires only internal constants (the per-edge Gauss order and the 500-evaluation ceiling); no public definition is named as retired or merged, and the section does not state why none can be.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — after the design the package carries three parallel polygon-moment bodies over the same machinery: separatrix_clip._traced_polygon_moments (geometric moments), clip_quadrature._straight_edge_monomial_moments (the production endpoint recurrence), and the new polygon_moments.polygon_monomial_moments; each hides its own reduction and none is the single owner, so the design added surface without adding depth.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — nova/equilibrium/separatrix_clip.py already owns polygon area/first/second moment integration (_traced_polygon_moments, line 850, JAX, orientation-aware) and nova/equilibrium/clip_quadrature.py owns the exact monomial table (_straight_edge_monomial_moments, line 155); the plan adds nova/equilibrium/polygon_moments.py as a third implementation rather than extending either owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 adds the public module nova/equilibrium/polygon_moments.py with five public symbols and its text names no public definition it retires or merges, nor why none can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 cites nova/biot/polygonanalytic.py polygon_analytic_flux_moments as the polygon-analytic machinery that "integrates the geometric moments of the region exactly", but that function (line 1787) computes flux-kernel blocks (G_0, G_R, G_Z) at target points, not area/first/second moments of a region; the geometric-moment owner the plan needs already exists as separatrix_clip._traced_polygon_moments (line 850) and is named in the reuse map comment but is not the mechanism the design extends.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the design replaces the fan quadrature with boundary integration rather than layering a thin pass-through over existing machinery; no unjustified wrapper is proposed.
